text.text_excerpt: Johnny Sanchez's happy hour has always been IT. I've been here quite a few times, but I hadn't visited in a while and stopped by yesterday evening because I was craving a solid margarita. The best perk: They had leftover Mardi Gras colored sugar for the margarita rims. And since I prefer sugar rims over salt, I loved the colorful addition! I also indulged in the $2 happy hour tacos, which were as tasty as ever. I got one Spicy Chicken taco consisting of crispy fried chicken, red chili glaze, pickled cucumber, pickled onion and one Des Allemands Fried Catfish taco topped with jalapeño tartar sauce and grilled corn salsa. Both were full of flavor, like all of their tacos! They have some of ...

I am happy to report that I had a fantastic experience at Johnny Sanchez. I don't know if it was the fact that I had a $50 gift card or if the drinks were making me giddy, but I left with a full belly and a big smile on my fat face. I'll start with the ambiance. We went for dinner at 8:30 on a Saturday night, so naturally the place was bumping. We were sat near the bar area, which was probably the only part I was meh about. My view was the backs of people at the bar and a room divider. The atmosphere was very fun and it was very lively, but I felt separated from the action. But nonetheless, 2 different types of salsas arrived at our table and I quickly got over my lack of people watching ...

The food was pretty good! The chips and salsa included plantain chips roasted in house and they were incredible! It definitely felt like upscale elevated Tex-Mex.The atmosphere was cool and funky, with unique light fixtures, a fun mural along with brightly colored chairs that really stood out against the more industrial style. A word of advice: the specialized tacos are pretty small so if you don't fill up on an appetizer, or are on the hungry side, you may want more than two. Our server was attentive, though not incredibly warm-- but hey maybe they were having a bad day, the food industry is tough so I understand.
